clue.text: Very tired club athlete

parts.note: shot is informal for worn out, exhausted
a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A sports star is utterly exhausted after a night at the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a nightclub or sports team but is the golf club used on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is a field-event competitor who hurls a heavy metal ball, so is an athlete.

clue.text: Casual get-together aboard cruise ship?

indicators.note: something aboard a vessel is carried inside it, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A relaxed party held on board a cruise liner.
explanation.walkthrough: SESH is slang short for session, as in a drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: A sesh is an informal slang word for a social session, often of drinking with friends.

clue.text: I know a smashing area somewhere in the Pacific

indicators.note: smashing breaks the words into pieces to be put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of knowing a wonderful spot out in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' poses as praise for the area but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is a Japanese island in the western Pacific Ocean, so it is a place out there.

clue.text: Inflexibility of editor involved in disastrous design phase

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it
something disastrous has gone badly wrong, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor's stubbornness wrecks a project's design stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of design phase make PIGHEADNESS, and ED is slotted in after PIGHEA to give PIGHEADEDNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig-headedness is obstinate stubbornness, a refusal to bend or change one's mind.

clue.text: Fish around river channel

indicators.note: around means one word is wrapped about the other

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Fish swim about in a river channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch or cut in the ground, a kind of channel.

clue.text: Stresses seem periodically to accompany developmental stages

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters
phases are stages of development

explanation.surface: Stress seems to recur at intervals as a child grows through each stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stresses' looks like a noun about pressure but is the plural of emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphases is the plural of emphasis, and a stress is an emphasis placed on a syllable or point.

clue.text: Hot show becomes a musical

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
to air something is to show or broadcast it

explanation.surface: A sizzling stage show is turned into a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is the 1960s rock musical about the hippie counterculture, an example of the genre.

clue.text: A tablet reconfigured for helping illegal activity

indicators.note: to reconfigure is to set up in a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A computer tablet is rigged to assist a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Abettal is the act of abetting, which means encouraging or assisting a wrongdoing.

clue.text: Being at ease takes skill and going back to square one

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside

parts.note: resting is relaxing, being at ease
an art is a skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Relaxing requires a knack, as does starting again from scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back to square one is an idiom for beginning again, which is what restarting means.

clue.text: Individual pocketing hard, small stones

indicators.note: pocketing something puts it away inside

parts.note: single means individual, one only
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone slips hard little pebbles into a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded pebbles, as found on many beaches.

clue.text: Staples possibly used for some Cassatt works

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Staples might have been used to mount some of Mary Cassatt's art.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Cassatt was an American Impressionist who made many of her best-known pictures in pastel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastels are pictures drawn with sticks of coloured chalk, a medium Cassatt used for many works.

clue.text: Certain characters seen in San Marino and Vatican City?

definitions.text: Certain characters seen in San Marino and Vatican City?

parts.note: surface reading: people you might meet in these places, or letters of type
setter's reading: both are tiny states whose chief city has the country's own name

explanation.surface: Wondering what sort of characters live in two tiny European states.
explanation.walkthrough: In typography the answer is capital letters set at lower-case height; the tiny states each serve as their own capital city, so they are literally little capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Small capitals are a typeface style, and the two microstates are diminutive capital cities.

clue.text: Fashion house manufactured a nice bag featuring a logo at the front

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw material, so these letters are formed anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: at the front points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A luxury label produces a handbag with its logo on the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Balenciaga is a Paris fashion house founded by the Spanish couturier Cristóbal Balenciaga.

clue.text: Leaves the bar, oddly

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered letters only

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone strangely walks out of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb but is a noun: tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea in its dry form is the cured leaves of the tea plant, sold loose or in bags.

clue.text: Support a government with a spread of information

parts.note: a prop is a support
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for government
and means together with
taken as written

explanation.surface: Backing a regime while disseminating facts about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is information, often biased, that is spread deliberately to promote a cause.

clue.text: Central components of forward country?

parts.note: surface reading: the key parts of a forward-looking nation; setter's reading: the three middle letters of the word forward
setter's reading: a nation in central Africa whose name begins with those three middle letters

explanation.surface: Asking what lies at the heart of a progressive nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle three letters of forward begin this landlocked central African country; the question mark admits that the rest of its name is not supplied, so the clue works only as a cryptic hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a small landlocked republic in east-central Africa, so it is a country.

clue.text: Accommodation on moorland proved to be a letdown

parts.note: a fell is a stretch of upland moor in northern England
a flat is an apartment, a place to live

explanation.surface: A holiday apartment on the moors turned out to be disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-the-page reading 'on' would put the first piece on top; here the accommodation is simply set after the moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall flat is an idiom for failing to have the hoped-for effect, as a joke that falls flat.

clue.text: Key bacteria finally found on dead mushroom

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: its last letter
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: A vital microbe turns up on a rotting fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mushroom' is a verb here, meaning to expand rapidly, not the fungus the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow quickly, and to escalate is to increase rapidly in scale or intensity.

clue.text: Heaven is located within a row of shops

indicators.note: located within means placed inside something else

parts.note: a parade is a row of shops, in British usage
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bliss is a high street with plenty of shops.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a parade is a short street or row of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a name for heaven, the blissful abode of the righteous after death.

clue.text: Novel about bishop heading off for holy city

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: re means about, concerning
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Mecca is Islam's holiest city

explanation.surface: A book about a bishop setting out on pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebecca is Daphne du Maurier's 1938 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is a well-known gothic novel by Daphne du Maurier, set at the house Manderley.

clue.text: Big-picture, ultimately utilitarian European leader

parts.note: macro describes the large-scale, overall view

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the following word

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A broad-visioned, practical head of government in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Macron is the president of France, so he is a leader in Europe.

clue.text: Was the lead singer a big stockholder?

parts.note: to run something is to lead it
Cher is a famous American singer

explanation.surface: Asking whether a band's frontman was also a major shareholder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stockholder' suggests shares, but the stock here is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher keeps large herds of cattle or other livestock, so holds a lot of stock.

clue.text: Salted nuts didn't run out

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The bowl of salted nuts never ran dry.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or endure, so something that lasted kept going without running out.

clue.text: Large amount of data about a talk

indicators.note: about means going round the outside

parts.note: GB is short for gigabyte
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lecture packed with heaps of statistics.
explanation.definitionFit: To gab is to chat idly at length, so it is an informal word meaning talk.

clue.text: Each country's restricting the onset of major emissions

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, enclosing from both sides

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: its first letter
read as nation is, or plural nations

explanation.surface: Every nation is curbing the start of serious pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s in 'country's' stands for 'is' in the surface, but the setter reads it as a plural, countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanations are things that flow or are given off from a source, so they are emissions.

clue.text: Pretentious group of people lacking power

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a party is a group of people
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A posy set who have no real influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone showily affecting artistic taste, which is a pretentious manner.

clue.text: Capital from independent firms invested in Northern Ireland and America

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it

parts.note: NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland
I is the abbreviation for independent
COS is short for companies
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Money from independent companies is put into Northern Ireland and the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, matching the investing scene, but is a capital city: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus, so it is a capital.

clue.text: Title mostly covering every single coaching role

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round something else
mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: a term is a name or designation for something
each means every single one

explanation.surface: Nearly every job title includes some coaching duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher instructs pupils, so teaching is a coaching role in the broad sense of tutoring.

clue.text: It contains antioxidants and saccharin occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A sweetener that sometimes comes with antioxidants.
explanation.walkthrough: Açaí is a Brazilian palm berry marketed as a superfood.
explanation.definitionFit: The acai berry is promoted as a health food rich in antioxidant compounds.

clue.text: Corrupt metal starts to affect smartphone charger?

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of the next words are taken

parts.note: first letters of both words
a charger is a large flat dish or platter

explanation.surface: A dodgy metal component damages a phone charger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charger' is not a phone accessory but an old word for a large serving platter.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt someone is to lead them astray, an idiom for tempting into wrongdoing.
